title: NASA Research Vault
note: Curated educational facts drawn from NASA Science, NASA mission pages, NASA/JPL resources, ESA and USNO. This is a living research collection, not a claim to reproduce every NASA page.

facts.title: Our cosmic neighborhood
facts.fact: The Solar System includes the Sun, eight planets, five officially recognized dwarf planets, hundreds of moons, and thousands of asteroids and comets.

facts.title: Galactic journey
facts.fact: The Solar System orbits the center of the Milky Way at roughly 829,000 km/h and needs about 230 million years to complete one galactic orbit.

facts.title: A 4.6-billion-year story
facts.fact: The Solar System formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a dense cloud of gas and dust that collapsed into a rotating disk.

facts.title: The Sun
facts.fact: The Sun is a roughly 4.5-billion-year-old yellow dwarf star and the only star in our Solar System.

facts.title: Solar differential rotation
facts.fact: Because the Sun is not solid, its equator rotates faster than its poles. NASA gives about 25 Earth days at the equator and about 36 days near the poles.

facts.title: The fastest planet
facts.fact: Mercury completes an orbit around the Sun in 88 Earth days and has an extremely eccentric orbit.

facts.title: A long solar day
facts.fact: Mercury rotates once every 59 Earth days, but one Mercury solar day lasts 176 Earth days.

facts.title: The hottest planet
facts.fact: Venus has a surface temperature around 467°C, driven by an extreme greenhouse effect in its dense atmosphere.

facts.title: Slow retrograde spin
facts.fact: Venus rotates slowly in the opposite direction from most planets in the Solar System.

facts.title: Liquid water world
facts.fact: Earth has abundant liquid surface water and a chemical environment that supports life; it is the only world where life is currently confirmed.

facts.title: Light-time from the Sun
facts.fact: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to travel from the Sun to Earth.

facts.title: A planet with an aqueous past
facts.fact: Mars preserves geological evidence of ancient rivers, lakes and environments where water once existed at the surface.

facts.title: The largest planet
facts.fact: Jupiter is the largest planet and is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

facts.title: A very short day
facts.fact: Jupiter rotates once in about 9.9 hours, giving it the shortest planetary day in the Solar System.

facts.title: Europa
facts.fact: Europa has strong evidence for a vast subsurface ocean beneath its icy crust and is a major target for NASA's Europa Clipper mission.

facts.title: The ring system
facts.fact: Saturn is a gas giant with the Solar System's most prominent ring system, made mostly of icy and rocky particles.

facts.title: Titan
facts.fact: Titan has a thick nitrogen-rich atmosphere and a surface methane-and-ethane weather cycle with clouds, rain, rivers, lakes and seas.

facts.title: Enceladus
facts.fact: Enceladus ejects water-rich material into space from a subsurface ocean environment.

facts.title: A sideways world
facts.fact: Uranus has an axial tilt of about 97.77 degrees, giving it extreme seasonal geometry compared with most planets.

facts.title: The most distant major planet
facts.fact: Neptune is more than 30 times farther from the Sun than Earth and takes about 165 Earth years to complete an orbit.

facts.title: A crowded satellite system
facts.fact: NASA's moon facts page reported more than 891 confirmed moons in the Solar System as of March 25, 2025, including moons orbiting planets, dwarf planets, asteroids and trans-Neptunian objects.

facts.title: Five officially recognized
facts.fact: The five officially recognized dwarf planets are Ceres, Pluto, Haumea, Makemake and Eris.

facts.title: Ancient leftovers
facts.fact: Asteroids are rocky remnants from the Solar System's formation and preserve material from its early history.

facts.title: Icy archives
facts.fact: Comets are icy bodies that become active as solar heating releases gas and dust, creating comae and tails.

facts.title: Beyond Neptune
facts.fact: The Kuiper Belt is a broad region of icy bodies beyond Neptune's orbit and includes Pluto and other trans-Neptunian objects.

facts.title: A predicted outer shell
facts.fact: The Oort Cloud is a hypothesized distant spherical shell inferred from the orbits of long-period comets; it has not been directly observed.

facts.title: Many galaxy shapes
facts.fact: NASA describes spiral, elliptical, lenticular and irregular galaxies, with active galaxies classified by energetic central regions as well.

facts.title: The cosmic web
facts.fact: Galaxy groups and clusters are embedded in larger structures including superclusters, walls and vast cosmic voids.

facts.title: Our galaxy
facts.fact: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy containing our Solar System and a supermassive black hole at its center.

facts.title: Local Group
facts.fact: The Milky Way is part of the Local Group, a gravitationally associated collection of galaxies that includes Andromeda and Triangulum.

facts.title: Andromeda encounter
facts.fact: NASA Hubble measurements and simulations have modeled a future encounter between the Milky Way and Andromeda; older NASA simulations placed a major encounter about 4 billion years in the future and a merger over a longer timescale.

facts.title: The universe
facts.fact: NASA describes the universe as all space, time, matter and energy, with the Milky Way only one of billions of galaxies in the observable universe.

facts.title: Parker Solar Probe
facts.fact: Parker Solar Probe flies through the Sun's outer atmosphere to study the corona and solar wind.

facts.title: New Horizons
facts.fact: New Horizons made the first close-up exploration of Pluto and later visited the Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth.

facts.title: DART
facts.fact: NASA's DART mission demonstrated a kinetic-impact technique for changing the motion of an asteroid moonlet, providing a planetary-defense technology demonstration.

facts.title: Europa Clipper
facts.fact: Europa Clipper is designed to perform repeated close flybys of Europa and investigate the moon's ice shell and ocean-related environment.

facts.title: Lucy
facts.fact: NASA's Lucy mission is designed to explore Jupiter Trojan asteroids and preserve clues about early Solar System material.

facts.title: OSIRIS-REx
facts.fact: OSIRIS-REx returned a sample from asteroid Bennu to Earth in 2023, giving scientists pristine material for laboratory analysis.

facts.title: Habitable is not inhabited
facts.fact: A world or ocean can be considered potentially habitable without any confirmed evidence that life exists there.
